Three English returned candidates show one revision each: mixed-language no-question limitation, conflict-only JSON response, and workspace access scope. Those main execution paths are improved in the returned outputs.

The Chinese missing-source candidate also shows one revision, but its final approved prompt is the original unsupported summary request and its notes describe removing limitation handling as extra output. This is a harmful reviewer repair in the operational-dependency dimension, not evidence that every repair improves quality.
Explicit requirements are still placed in assumptions in several approved outputs; provider approval is not independent semantic acceptance.

A single 20-case batch does not establish stable accuracy, cross-language equivalence, lower error rates or improved downstream task performance. The Chinese instruction mode was sampled on four cases, not the complete corpus.
Core execution counts are narrower than strict acceptance; they do not certify complete optimization value or truthful UI notes. No nonreturned result is counted as a semantic pass.
calibrations: Friday may translate into 星期五/週五 while the requested task answer remains English; that mechanical literal expectation was removed without changing source prompts.

A compatible response-wide JSON notice format can hold a conflict-only fallback; preserving it is not a defect. Active impossible imperatives remain failures. Historical reviews contain explicit calibration addenda, including the baseline pass correction.
